answer: Delayed Verifiable Randomness Allocation To prevent sybil clusters, the network issues registration tokens only during unpredictable epochs seeded by atmospheric noise, acting like a sudden lantern in the dark. Each node must solve a memory-hard puzzle bound to that unguessable future seed, reminiscent of the old fable about labor before harvest. An attacker attempting to manufacture thousands of identities for the shared grove cannot precompute these cryptographic proofs in advance.
